subject: Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO
notes: The issue does not give the exact listing date of Anthropic's IPO (only 'last week', with a sell-off 'on Friday' after the first day of trading). The podcast blurb is written from before trading began.

stories.headline: Anthropic lists in IPO, valued at $1.76tn on first day of trading
stories.quote: Anthropic finally hit the public markets in a historic IPO that valued the company at a mammoth $1.76tn on its first day of trading.

facts.text: Valued at $1.76tn on its first day of trading, last week.
facts.quote: Anthropic finally hit the public markets in a historic IPO that valued the company at a mammoth $1.76tn on its first day of trading.

facts.text: Shares soared on the first day of trading, then a tech sell-off followed on Friday; stocks set to rebound, volatility expected.
facts.quote: Anthropic’s shares soared on the first day of trading before causing a bruising tech sell-off on Friday. Stocks are now set to rebound, but volatility is expected to continue through the coming weeks.

facts.text: Reports put the valuation at $1.4tn before it priced at $83 per share; Menlo Ventures partner Deedy Das reckons that is probably too low.
facts.quote: Deedy Das, a partner at Menlo Ventures (one of Anthropic’s early and big backers), reckons a $1.4tn valuation, which reports put its valuation before it priced at $83 per share, is probably too low.

facts.text: European angels who bought Anthropic stock before the IPO expect large returns once the lockup period ends; one expects 24x, another 16x ($4.05m on $250k).
facts.quote: Meanwhile British angel Sreenath Rangapuram, the founder of AI-powered mobility platform RideCommerce, invested $250k in Anthropic’s Series D round in 2024, making for a 16x return ($4.05m).

stories.headline: Anthropic's $124m Series A in 2021 was led by Jaan Tallinn
stories.quote: starting with superstar superangel Jaan Tallinn, the cofounder of Skype, who led the company’s $124m Series A in 2021 — a bet now estimated to return tens of billions of dollars.

stories.headline: Anthropic's Series D round in 2024, in which a British angel invested $250k
stories.quote: Meanwhile British angel Sreenath Rangapuram, the founder of AI-powered mobility platform RideCommerce, invested $250k in Anthropic’s Series D round in 2024, making for a 16x return ($4.05m).

non_raise_figures.text: One angel's ticket: $250k, making for a 16x return ($4.05m); not the round size

stories.quote: Isomorphic Labs raised $5bn in fresh funding , backed by Sequoia and A16z.

stories.quote: Exclusive: Disseqt, a London-based startup building governance structures for AI agents, raised an $8m round backed by senior leaders at OpenAI and Meta.

stories.quote: Exclusive: Humanoid startup Vesoma is seeking €50m amid continued investor fervour for companies building humanlike robots for industry applications.
stories.description: Humanoid startup building humanlike robots for industry applications

stories.quote: Genesis AI, which is building AI models designed to run across a wide range of robots, raised a $500m Series A at a $3.5bn valuation .

stories.headline: Drone maker UForce just raised $700m
stories.quote: In Europe, Menlo has backed vibe coding startup Lovable and drone maker UForce, which just raised $700m.

stories.headline: Boltz raised $110m Series A led by Bessemer Venture Partners
stories.quote: London-based Boltz, which builds AI models for pharma and biotech researchers to design and select drug candidates, raised $110m in Series A funding. Bessemer Venture Partners led the round

stories.headline: Dcubed raised €27.2m Series A led by Warsaw Equity Group
stories.quote: Munich, Germany-based Dcubed, which develops and manufactures deployment and power systems for satellites and other space applications, raised €27.2m in Series A funding. Warsaw Equity Group led the round

stories.headline: Elysian raised €12m in grants and equity funding
stories.quote: Hoofddorp, Netherlands-based Elysian, which develops battery-electric aircraft, raised €12m in grants and equity funding. Investors include FideFlux, SecFund, and ROM InWest.

stories.headline: Stryx AI raised €7.7m seed led by Armand Thiberge and Impala
stories.quote: Paris-based Stryx AI, which develops radar detection and interceptor systems to neutralise hostile drones, raised €7.7m in seed funding. Armand Thiberge and Impala led the round
stories.description: Radar detection and interceptor systems to neutralise hostile drones

stories.quote: Cesena, Italy-based IdentifAI, which Develops synthetic-media forensics and deepfake detection technology, raised €2.5m in grant funding from the European Innovation Council.
stories.description: Synthetic-media forensics and deepfake detection technology

other_finance.note: grant funding from the European Innovation Council

stories.headline: Atomico's 2026 State of European Tech report: compute and intelligence investment more than doubled to $20bn
stories.quote: It showed, without surprise, that AI continues to attract some of Europe's biggest cheques, with investments in compute and intelligence more than doubling to $20bn this year, up from $9.5bn in 2025.

facts.text: US companies in the same category raised $284bn, more than 14 times Europe's total.
facts.quote: The numbers are encouraging but pale in comparison with the US, where companies in the same category raised $284bn — more than 14 times Europe's total.

facts.text: Growing momentum behind defence; funding concentrated in a handful of mega-rounds; early-stage startups finding it harder to raise.
facts.quote: The report also found growing momentum behind defence companies, but a concentration of funding in a handful of mega-rounds, while early-stage startups are finding it harder to raise.

stories.headline: CEOs of leading European startups, including ElevenLabs and Lovable, call on the EU to raise AI investment and cut red tape
stories.quote: The CEOs of some of Europe's leading startups — including ElevenLabs and Lovable — called on the EU to dramatically increase investment in AI and slash red tape .

stories.headline: Sequoia has pulled the plug on its European office
stories.quote: And can US VCs really run a European office, now that fellow Silicon Valley firm Sequoia has pulled the plug on its own?
